chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Isma'il ibn Marar from Yunus from Ya'qub ibn Shu'ayb al-Athmi said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'There is no harm for the Mutamatti' (one performing Hajj al-Tamattu') if he does not enter the state of Ihram from the night of Tarwiyah, whenever it is convenient for him, as long as he does not fear missing the two standings (of Arafat and Muzdalifah).'

key_terms.الْمَوْقِفَيْنِ: The two standings (at Arafat and Muzdalifah)
key_terms.لَيْلَةِ التَّرْوِيَةِ: The night of Tarwiyah (8th of Dhu al-Hijjah)
key_terms.لِلْمُتَمَتِّعِ: For the one performing Tamattu' (a type of Hajj)

ai.seo_question: When can a pilgrim performing Hajj al-Tamattu' enter the state of Ihram?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the flexibility of the Hajj al-Tamattu' by permitting the pilgrim to delay entering the state of Ihram until the night of Tarwiyah, as long as the essential standing at Arafat and Muzdalifah is not jeopardized. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on practical ease (taysir) within the framework of ritual validity, distinguishing the Tamattu' mode from the continuous Ihram of Qiran or Ifrad.
